column2: the prefetch window counts raw issue rows instead of title-prefixed bugs, so a single `gh issue list --limit n` call can underfill the audit or miss older bugs.
git evidence and deep verification can read the wrong ref when the checkout is not exactly main.
the new runtime entrypoint needs to follow the repo's package and cli import model, not a flat root module.
the deep-verifier model flag has no real dispatch path, so non-sonnet choices are ignored and the public cli lies about model selection.
when local grep misses a fix commit, the pr fallback still needs a merge commit to build bundles and ledger keys.
the cap needs a fixed priority order and explicit overflow behavior when required candidates exceed the limit.
sampled deep checks need distinct provenance and false-pass metrics so the calibration run is measurable.
cached runs must not skip unfinished stages, and malformed stripping must not be cached as clean evidence.
cache keys and append-only ingest need deterministic rules so duplicate or ambiguous rows do not change resume behavior.
the bug corpus can still be built from open issues only, so closed [bug] fixes may never enter the audit.
the `--deep-model` alias path still needs one concrete mapping that governs verifier dispatch and pricing, or the run can validate one tier while charging another.
the skill still lacks an explicit stdout/argv handoff for durable run and ledger paths, so resumed stages can read stale artifacts.
reporting by issue number alone can resurrect stale cached verdicts for reopened bugs or changed fix surfaces; the merge must respect the full cache key triple.
`--sample k` needs to draw only from fixed triage verdicts eligible for false-pass measurement, not arbitrary or already-deep-queued rows.
a substring `git log --grep` match can bind the wrong fix commit to a bug.
the triage and deep agents still do not pin the ingestable jsonl fields, so the ledger cannot reliably validate or join their output.
